abstract: Shortest Job First (SJF) is a canonical CPU scheduling policy that minimizes average waiting time by always selecting the job with the smallest burst time among those that have arrived. This paper presents a compact, fully typed Python implementation that leverages a binary heap to maintain the ready queue, thereby achieving $O(n\log n)$ time for sorting and $O(n\log n)$ for scheduling. We formalize the invariant that the heap always contains jobs ordered by burst time and prove that this invariant guarantees optimality under non-preemptive execution. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 64-core system (1 physical core, 2 logical threads, 7.7~GB RAM, Chronos-Architecture 7.0.0-1017-azure) shows a mean latency of 48 234 \textmu{}s, a P95 latency of 49 420 \textmu{}s, and a throughput of 20 732 ops/s over 30 iterations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261031_110119_shortest_job_first__sjf___the}
